No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not prove complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; permit only bounded reversible work that preserves existing consent, disclosures, data handling, claims, and platform-policy boundaries. Continue existing read-only evidence work using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Do not access credentials or private containers, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, expand alerts, or conduct external outreach. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, medium for bounded reversible growth. This is not a penetration test, certification, or clean bill of health.

Retain the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix. Record dated, redacted evidence and owners for authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not create duplicate requests or production work.
